text:
I don't know how it happens, but almost every time, exactly one minute before an important call, my son announces, "Mommy... I've pooped."

I've realized that almost every meeting starts with some version of poop. Sometimes it's your report. Sometimes it's my design.

I'm lucky to work at a company where no one loses their shit over real-life events. Life doesn't pause just because we're at work: kids still poop, dogs bark, deliveries arrive, and AI releases another model that makes designers question their entire careers.

One thing Nick Gluzdov once told me has stayed with me ever since: "Turn off your AI wallpaper. I want to see your background." At first, I thought he meant my room. Now I think he meant something bigger. He didn’t want me to hide my real life.

Lately, I've been quietly freaking out about how quickly AI is reshaping design. Some days, I feel like everything I've spent years learning is being rewritten overnight. But then my son reminds me that life is still happening outside my screen.

One day, he'll stop needing me to rescue him after every poop. And one day, I'll probably stop panicking every time AI changes the rules again.

Next week, I'm starting a new design course, not because I think I'll ever explore every single AI feature Figma releases, but because I'd like to spend less time shitting myself about AI and more time learning how to work with it.

I'll share what I learn along the way in case it helps anyone else who's trying to keep up with AI while remembering there's still a life to live.

comments.text:
Oh, this touches the soul (and my survival instincts) so deeply! As a mom of an 8-year-old now, let me give you a spoiler alert: the "pre-call emergency poop" phase does end, but it just gets replaced by a kid standing silently in the dark of your room at 2 AM to tell you they lost a Lego piece😂

You’re so righ: the real magic happens when we turn off the "AI wallpaper" and embrace the messy, unedited background. AI might be updating its models every five minutes and making us question our careers, but it will never match the chaotic brilliance of real life. Love your honesty, and good luck with the new course! Let's face Figma and the chaos together 🚀
